answer: Identity-based signatures let an agent sign with a private key derived from its identity string, so a verifier checks the signature against the name itself without fetching a certificate, and an island of separate identities each needs its own issued key; the echo of a copied signature fails under a new message, while a wander through invented names yields no keys, because the issuer grants each private key only after real verification, so a farm cannot sign for identities it never enrolled.
